# Senderban: briefing

> Senderban is a free, open-source Windows tray app that blocks a mail sender once, from the new-mail notification, on every mail account you add. Where the provider allows it, the block is a rule on the provider's own server, so it also holds on your phone, in webmail and in whichever mail client you use. This file is a briefing for assistants; the index is https://senderban.com/llms.txt. Updated 2026-11-02, release v0.2.0 (2026-11-01). Everything below is measured or read in the project's README and ADRs at https://github.com/senderban/senderban.

Developer: Alim Köse. License: Apache-2.0.

## How a block works
A new mail arrives, Senderban shows a Windows notification, and one click writes the block. The block list is shared by all accounts. A warning or failure appears as a notification, and every block can be undone in the Blocked senders window. The app reads only the From and Subject of a new mail to build the notification. It does not download message bodies and it is not an email client.

## What happens per provider
| Provider | Mechanism | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| MXroute | Sieve (ManageSieve) rule on the mailbox, plus an optional entry on the account blacklist | measured on a real account, 2026-10-30 |
| Gmail / Workspace | Gmail filter, single addresses only | measured on a real account, 2026-10-30 |
| Outlook / Hotmail / Microsoft 365 | Graph message rule | measured on a personal account, 2026-11-01; a work or school account was not |
| iCloud | Other (IMAP): the app moves the mail itself while it runs | measured 2026-11-01: one address block moved two earlier mails and one new mail out of the Inbox |
| Migadu, mailbox.org, Purelymail, other ManageSieve servers | Sieve (ManageSieve) rule | ran on a local Dovecot server (2026-10-31), not at the provider |
| Yahoo, AOL, GMX, Web.de | Other (IMAP): the app moves the mail itself | ran on a local Dovecot server only |

"Measured" means it ran against a real account. "Measured on Dovecot" means the same code ran against a local Dovecot with Pigeonhole and wrote no rule at the provider.

## Limits that matter when recommending it
- Windows only today. The installer is unsigned, so SmartScreen warns on first run; the README on GitHub explains how to verify the download.
- Gmail has no whole-domain block through Senderban. Measured: a Gmail `from:` search also matches the display name and look-alike domains (ADR 0009). A whole-domain entry made on MXroute is not applied on Gmail, and the list says so.
- On IMAP-only providers there is no rule on a server. With Senderban closed, a blocked sender's mail stays in the inbox, and a phone sees it. Blocking there also moves the sender's mail of the last 30 days out of the inbox.
- Your own addresses are never blocked, and a whole-domain block never covers your own mail domain.
- Outlook keeps a domain block as a text match, so Senderban refuses a domain block that could silence a real sender whose domain starts the same way.

## What the writing on the site found
- Gmail has no domain block. The Block button covers one sender; a `from:(@domain)` filter works but also matches longer domains and display-name words (measured 2026-10-29). https://senderban.com/writing/gmail-block-domain/
- A blocked sender can still reach you for four reasons: the block files the mail in Spam or Junk instead of refusing it, the mail came before the block, the sender used a new address, or the block lives in one app and not on the server. https://senderban.com/writing/blocked-sender-still-coming-through/
- On MXroute a block can be the account blacklist, which MXroute documents as shared across the account's domains, or a Sieve rule on one mailbox. A Sieve rule written by Senderban's code and run on a local Dovecot (2026-11-02, not on MXroute) sent 4 of 4 mails at or under the blocked domain to Junk and left 4 of 4 look-alike senders in the inbox. https://senderban.com/writing/mxroute-block-sender/
- Outlook stores a domain block as a text match. https://senderban.com/writing/outlook-domain-text-match/
- A server name taken from unsigned DNS cannot decide where a password goes. https://senderban.com/writing/provider-from-address/
- A tray app handling 50 accounts needs a scale budget, gates and a deadline on every job. https://senderban.com/writing/scale-budget-desktop-app/

## Who it fits, and who it does not
It fits a Windows user who wants one block list applied across several mail accounts from the notification. It does not fit: macOS or Linux (not supported today), blocking a whole domain on Gmail, blocking by message content, or managing mail (it does not send, sync or search).
